newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish FinMin says committee to mull EMU needs.
newsitem.headline: Swedish FinMin says committee to mull EMU needs.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Thursday the question of whether there must be constitutional changes for Sweden's eventual entrance into the EMU would be sent to a new committee for consideration.
"The proposal to send the issue out for consideration was put at this meeting and we agreed to do that," Asbrink said after a meeting of Swedish parliamentary leaders.
He said a group of representatives from all of the parties would be set up to look at this issue.
"We have time to think about how we will act. There are different understandings also among lawyers," he told reporters.
Asbrink said he understood that Sweden's eventual entrance to EMU would be a political decision.
To make any changes to Sweden's constitution, there needs to be two parliamentary votes of approval with a general election between the two votes.
Sweden's next general election is scheduled for September 1998.
